title: I was WRONG about these lifts
summary: NH publicly reverses his stance on five lifts: weighted dips, JM press, heel-elevated squats and the Smith machine, side bends and incline curls. For each he explains where his reasoning went wrong (theory over practice, elitist dogma, misplaced safety fears) and gives cues and rep ranges. He frames admitting mistakes as essential to growth.
claims: It's only wrong to be wrong when you refuse to accept it; influencers who hide their reversals teach lifters to fear mistakes
Weighted dips are not inherently dangerous; pain usually comes from poor shoulder mobility, so fix the mobility instead of blaming the lift
Young lifters with sternum pain while still developing shouldn't push through dips
Avoiding dips and doubling down on bench is where shoulder injuries happen; dips would protect you
The weighted dip is the 'squat of the upper body', S-tier for chest, triceps and shoulders; novices starting with dips instead of bench would build better physiques
Dips humble you and discourage ego lifting more than bench does
The JM press is S-tier: it feels like a triceps-only close-grip press, not a skull crusher
The JM press is easy on the elbows, a tendon builder; NH cured his elbow tendinitis with it, following arm wrestler Todd Hutchings' advice
SSB without handles and the Smith machine are ideal for JM presses; the Smith version is the triceps isolation he can push hardest to true failure
Heel elevation isn't for poor mobility only; with something under the heels it removes ankle mobility limits and lets the knees travel forward for deeper quad range
Saying high-bar or heel-elevated squats aren't 'real' squats is childish elitist powerlifting dogma
Smith machine test: an influencer who says the Smith machine isn't for real men isn't worth following
Removing stability demands (Smith) or grip (straps) lets you hit the target muscle harder, not less
Even with ass-to-grass mobility, hamstrings hitting calves limit depth; heel elevation lets the quads reach failure
About 80% of NH's squat volume is now heel-elevated at 20-45 degrees
Heel-elevated squats give more effective range, less lower-back strain and a better stimulus-to-fatigue ratio
Side bends are an S-tier oblique and whole-core builder if you bend fully to each side; NH wrongly believed lateral spinal flexion was dangerous
Train a lift seriously for at least 3 months before judging it
Do side bends one side at a time; rotating-collar Olympic dumbbells roll smoothly along the body; elevate one side or use a hyperextension bench to make them harder
Incline curls are an A/S-tier biceps exercise; his earlier C-tier rating was wrong because he relied on theory over practice
With a controlled negative, incline curl momentum extends the stretch, where the biggest hypertrophic response occurs
Bad strength curves create grinds, and grinding is where the muscle works hardest; the JM press with an SSB is the same
To grind incline curls, keep the elbow tucked and the hand supinated near 45 degrees instead of committing the elbow forward
You can rest-pause incline curls at the top with elbow and forearm stacked for 10-15 s to get 2-3 extra reps past failure
Incline curls are hard to progress for two reasons: too little intensity to move up in weight, or too little volume to acclimate; use 6-12 reps
Use a false (thumbless) grip on incline curls to lock in supination and stop the wrist taking over
Don't do incline curls on a cable; use Bayesian curls for a cable-aligned strength curve
Steve Reeves did incline curls with dumbbells on a slight incline
The day a man thinks he is done learning is the day he dies
exercises: respect it, no ego lifting; fix shoulder mobility
upper-body squat for chest, triceps, shoulders
press with triceps only, touch at neck or nose level, elbows stacked; SSB or Smith
triceps builder and elbow tendon rehab
deeper quad ROM, quads reach failure, less lower back
removes stability demand to target muscles
full range each side, one side at a time, rotating-collar dumbbells, elevated or hyperextension-bench variants
control the negative, elbow tucked, supinate through pinky, false grip, rest at top for extra reps, 6-12
cable alternative instead of cable incline curls
